title: The Group Chat of the water tower
premise: Felix Almeida just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built atop the ruins of a 1950s reform school. But when the legendary water tower ghost begins leaving him handwritten notes in ink that no pen could produce, he learns the ghost is a student who died there decades ago — and that the school's beloved founding family covered up her death. As Felix and his new friends decode the notes, they uncover that the cover-up never ended: the current principal, a descendant of the founders, has been burying similar incidents for years. The truth comes out the night of prom, when Felix chooses exposing the history over protecting his best friend's family name, ending with the school board forced to acknowledge the buried dead and Felix finally counting days toward something instead of away from it.
about_author: Wendell Reyes is a former night-shift security guard at three different converted schools, a job that gave him an enduring fondness for buildings that remember too much. He writes young adult fiction from a small apartment full of archived yearbooks he refuses to explain.

chapters.title: Ninety-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On his first day at Hollow Creek High, Felix catalogs exits, cliques, and the countdown to graduation, determined to stay invisible until June. A tour guide mentions the water tower ghost as a joke. Emotional beat: weary detachment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Tower
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. During detention spent cleaning the auditorium, Felix sees a figure on the roofline near the water tower — gone when he blinks. His deskmate Priya insists everyone sees her once. Emotional beat: skepticism cracking into unease.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He finds a note in his locker reading 'FELIX ALMEIDA — YOU COUNT DAYS. I COUNT YEARS.' The ink shimmers wet but leaves nothing on his fingers. Priya witnesses it and goes pale. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya lays out the ghost lore: the girl only contacts people who are 'unclaimed' — friendless, new, overlooked. She warns Felix to ignore the notes; the last kid who answered transferred out mid-year. Emotional beat: protective anxiety.

chapters.title: Marisol Vance, 1958
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the library's restricted local-history shelf, Felix finds a 1958 yearbook with one photo razored out and Marisol Vance's name scratched from every club roster. Someone went to great trouble to erase her. Emotional beat: quiet outrage.

chapters.title: The Founders' Wing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Principal Whitlock Almeida — Felix's distant cousin by coincidence of surname — gives Felix a personal welcome and a scholarship offer contingent on 'representing the school's legacy.' Felix notices the founders' portraits all share Whitlock's jaw. Emotional beat: flattered, then watched.

chapters.title: Dex Makes It a Group Chat
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Chaotic, loyal Dex drags Felix and Priya into a group chat named GHOST SQUAD and proposes they answer the next note together. The ghost replies within minutes, addressing all three by name. Emotional beat: giddy terror becoming belonging.

chapters.title: What the Notes Ask
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The notes shift from riddles to requests: find the tower's maintenance hatch key, photograph the cornerstone, don't tell Whitlock. Each completed task reveals another erased detail of Marisol's life. Emotional beat: complicity deepening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Cornerstone
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Behind the 1959 cornerstone, the trio finds a tin box: Marisol's diary pages describing abuse at the reform school and a fire she planned to expose. The last page names her attacker only as 'W.A.' Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of proof.

chapters.title: Whitlock Knows
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Whitlock summons Felix, returns the scholarship paperwork, and casually mentions the library's restricted shelf was relocked after his visit. The message is unmistakable. Emotional beat: the trap of comfort versus conscience.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Dex, running prom logistics, discovers Whitlock controls the venue, budget, and guest list — leverage over every student. Meanwhile Felix's scholarship acceptance sits unsigned on his desk. Emotional beat: realizing power works through small favors.

chapters.title: Split the Squad
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya wants to take the diary to a journalist; Felix wants to wait until after graduation; Dex wants to protect his brother, who works for Whitlock. The group chat goes silent for the first time. Emotional beat: loyalty straining against strategy.

chapters.title: The Fire Drill That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A midnight alarm empties the school; when students return, Felix's locker is clean — every note gone. Whitlock stands in the doorway of the empty room like he's been waiting. Emotional beat: violation and the loss of evidence.

chapters.title: Cold Ink
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. For six days, silence. Then a single note appears on Felix's windshield, written not in shimmering ink but ordinary ballpoint: 'She can't reach you anymore. Can you still reach her?' Emotional beat: grief for a friendship with the dead.

chapters.title: Dex's Brother Talks
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Dex's brother admits Whitlock paid him to copy the group chat and search the tower hatch. He also lets slip that Whitlock keeps a private archive in the founders' wing basement. Emotional beat: guilt converting into defiance.

chapters.title: The Basement Archive
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Using prom-night access schedules, the trio maps the basement: incident reports from 1994, 2003, 2016 — each a student hurt, each report signed W. Almeida and sealed. The cover-up is a family tradition. Emotional beat: horror scaling from past to present.

chapters.title: Seventeen Days
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. With prom seventeen days out, Whitlock offers Felix everything: guaranteed college letter, his mother's medical bills quietly handled — if he graduates clean and forgets Marisol. Felix looks at the unsigned acceptance and finally understands what being bought feels like. Emotional beat: temptation at its most human.

chapters.title: The Note in Marisol's Hand
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The ghost returns one last time, leaving a page in Marisol's own voice: not vengeance, but a request to be counted — named, remembered, entered into the record. Felix signs the group chat's founding rule: nobody carries this alone. Emotional beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: Prom Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. During prom, while Whitlock gives his toast, the trio triggers the fire alarm — then, instead of fleeing, projects the archive documents onto the gymnasium screen and reads Marisol's name aloud. Emotional beat: the point of no return, chosen together.

chapters.title: What the Water Tower Saw
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Chaos, denial, and then corroboration: the 2016 victim, now a teacher, steps forward publicly. Whitlock suspends Felix pending expulsion. Walking out past the water tower, Felix feels watched — kindly, this time. Emotional beat: cost accepted without regret.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At the school board hearing, students testify in relay so no single voice can be dismissed; Dex's brother hands over copies he made before returning the originals. The board votes to open an independent investigation and restore Marisol Vance's name to the records. Emotional beat: justice assembled from ordinary courage.

chapters.title: Zero Days
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Graduation day. Marisol's name is read alongside the class as an honorary graduate, and the last note in Felix's locker is a single word in impossible ink: 'Free.' He deletes the countdown app and starts a group chat with a new name. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into beginning.
